meta.indication: prevention of major coronary events after acute coronary syndrome (randomized within 30 days of ACS hospitalization)

n_randomized.quote: SOLID-TIMI 52 was a multinational, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial that randomized 13,026 participants within 30 days of hospitalization with an ACS (non-ST-elevation or ST-elevation myocardial infarction [MI]) at 868 sites in 36 countries.

median_followup.quote: Patients were followed up for a median of 2.5 years between December 7, 2009, and December 6, 2013.
median_followup.note: 2.5 years = 30 months. Design anticipated median treatment ~3 years (S2).

primary_endpoint.value: Major coronary events: CHD death, MI, or urgent coronary revascularization for myocardial ischemia (amended Dec 2013; originally CV death, MI, or stroke)
primary_endpoint.quote: The prior secondary end point of major coronary events (CHD death, MI, or urgent coronary revascularization for myocardial ischemia) became the primary end point of the trial.
primary_endpoint.note: Design paper S2 (2011) and original protocol: primary = CV death, nonfatal MI, nonfatal stroke. Amended in December 2013 after the executive committee reviewed STABILITY results, before SOLID unblinding: 'In December 2013, the SOLID-TIMI 52 executive committee reviewed data from the recently completed STABILITY trial prior to the unblinding or closure of the SOLID-TIMI 52 database.' Quotes obtained via WebFetch of JAMA full text.

inclusion_key_criteria.value: Hospitalization for ACS (NSTEMI or STEMI) within 30 days, plus >=1 additional risk predictor (age >=60, prior MI, diabetes on medication, mild/moderate renal impairment, cerebrovascular or peripheral artery disease)
inclusion_key_criteria.quote: Hospitalization for acute coronary syndrome (ACS) within 30 days prior to study entry.
inclusion_key_criteria.note: Registry lists the additional risk factors: at least 60 years old; MI prior to qualifying ACS; diabetes requiring medication; mild or moderate reduction in kidney function; cerebrovascular disease or peripheral artery disease.

planned_events.quote: When the study was initially designed, it was determined that 1500 events would be required to yield 90% power to detect a 15.5% reduction in the risk of the primary end point (HR = 0.845)
planned_events.note: Planned for the ORIGINAL primary end point (MACE). JAMA: 'The number of reported primary end point events was relatively comparable under both definitions and therefore the end point change did not substantially affect the power to evaluate the primary hypothesis.' Observed MCE events 1813 (903+910). Design abstract S2 (2011): 'approximately 1,500 primary end point events ... 90% power to detect a 15.5% reduction'.

assumed_rrr.quote: When the study was initially designed, it was determined that 1500 events would be required to yield 90% power to detect a 15.5% reduction in the risk of the primary end point (HR = 0.845)

power.quote: When the study was initially designed, it was determined that 1500 events would be required to yield 90% power to detect a 15.5% reduction in the risk of the primary end point (HR = 0.845)

alpha.quote: On the basis of 2 planned interim analyses, the primary end point was assessed at a threshold of significance of P value less than .049 after applying a flexible α-spending function.
alpha.note: Quote obtained via WebFetch of JAMA full text; registry CI level 95.02%.

stopped_early.quote: Patients were followed up for a median of 2.5 years between December 7, 2009, and December 6, 2013.

baseline.quote: Lp-PLA2 activity, median IQR, nmol/min/mL: 172.5 (142.7-208.0) darapladib; 174.4 (143.7-208.2) placebo
baseline.note: Table values, quote reconstructed from table row via WebFetch; placebo 174.4.

biomarker_effects.quote: the 160-mg dose of darapladib is anticipated to achieve an approximate 66% reduction in Lp-PLA2 activity on a background of statin therapy.
biomarker_effects.note: NOT FOUND: no measured on-treatment Lp-PLA2 activity reported in the SOLID-TIMI 52 JAMA paper (only the anticipated ~66%, citing phase 2). Pooled darapladib trials: Gregson 2017 (S11) '160 mg once-daily darapladib reduced Lp-PLA2 activity by 65%' (secondary systematic review, not SOLID-specific).

biomarker_effects.quote: Darapladib 40, 80, and 160 mg inhibited Lp-PLA(2) activity by approximately 43%, 55%, and 66% compared with placebo (p < 0.001 weeks 4 and 12).
biomarker_effects.note: Stable CHD/risk-equivalent patients on atorvastatin, n=959.

biomarker_effects.quote: At 12 weeks, darapladib 160 mg decreased interleukin (IL)-6 by 12.3% (95% confidence interval [CI] -22% to -1%; p = 0.028) and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) by 13.0% (95% CI -28% to +5%; p = 0.15) compared with placebo.
In contrast, Lp-PLA(2) activity was inhibited by 59% with darapladib (P<0.001 versus placebo).
biomarker_effects.note: IBIS-2; primary end points negative; necrotic core -5.2 mm3 (secondary, P=0.012).

hr.quote: the primary end point occurred in 903 patients in the darapladib group and 910 in the placebo group (16.3% vs 15.6% at 3 years; hazard ratio [HR], 1.00 [95% CI, 0.91-1.09]; P = .93)

events_treatment.quote: the primary end point occurred in 903 patients in the darapladib group

safety_signals.quote: Patients were more likely to report an odor-related concern in the darapladib group vs the placebo group (11.5% vs 2.5%) and also more likely to report diarrhea (10.6% vs 5.6%).
safety_signals.note: AE leading to study drug discontinuation 17% vs 12% (JAMA full text via WebFetch).

safety_signals.value: Original primary end point (CV death, MI, stroke) also null
safety_signals.quote: The composite of cardiovascular death, MI, or stroke occurred in 824 in the darapladib group and 838 in the placebo group (15.0% vs 15.0% at 3 years; HR, 0.99 [95% CI, 0.90-1.09]; P = .78).
safety_signals.note: Efficacy, recorded because it was the original primary end point.

safety_signals.quote: all-cause mortality (371 events in the darapladib group and 395 in the placebo group [7.3% vs 7.1% at 3 years; HR, 0.94 [95% CI, 0.82-1.08]; P = .40)

genetics.finding: PLA2G7 V279F (loss-of-function, 'm' allele) was MORE frequent in Japanese patients with MI or stroke than in controls (candidate-gene case-control, n=3932); direction opposite to the darapladib hypothesis
genetics.effect: qualitative; no effect size in abstract
genetics.quote: We observed a significantly increased frequency of the m allele in the diseased group as compared with the control or risk-factor groups.
genetics.note: Small early East Asian candidate-gene study; abstract read on PubMed. Later East Asian V279F studies were pooled in Gregson 2017.

genetics.finding: Common PLA2G7 variants have only small effects on Lp-PLA2 activity (weak instrument) and showed no association with CHD; authors state they could not exclude a modest causal effect
genetics.effect: rs1051931 (A379V) VV vs AA: +7.2% Lp-PLA2 activity; CHD events OR 0.98 (95% CI 0.82-1.17); angiographic CAD OR 1.03 (0.80-1.32)
genetics.quote: Genotype was not associated with risk markers, angiographic coronary disease (odds ratio, 1.03; 95% confidence interval, 0.80 to 1.32), or CHD events (odds ratio, 0.98; 95% confidence interval, 0.82 to 1.17).
genetics.note: Weak-instrument caveat in the Discussion (PMC author manuscript): 'a per-allele OR as low as 1.05 (which we were insufficiently powered to detect) could still be compatible with a contributory role of Lp-PLA2 to CHD.' Abstract also: 'Larger association studies, identification of single-nucleotide polymorphisms with larger effects, or randomized trials of specific Lp-PLA2 inhibitors are needed'.

genetics.finding: PLA2G7 V279F loss-of-function variant (lifelong lower Lp-PLA2) not associated with major vascular events or major coronary events in 91,428 China Kadoorie Biobank participants
genetics.effect: Major vascular events OR 0.98 per F allele (95% CI 0.90-1.06); major coronary events OR 0.96 (0.79-1.18)
genetics.quote: V279F was not associated with major vascular events [7141 events; odds ratio (OR) = 0.98 per F variant, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.90-1.06] or other vascular outcomes, including major coronary events (922 events; 0.96, 0.79-1.18) and stroke (5967 events; 1.00, 0.92-1.09).
genetics.note: Published in Int J Epidemiol (not JAMA Cardiol); post-dates both darapladib readouts.

genetics.finding: Large-scale genetic invalidation: none of five Lp-PLA2-lowering PLA2G7 alleles associated with CHD; genetic causal risk ratio per 65% lower Lp-PLA2 activity matches the null darapladib trial estimate
genetics.effect: CHD RR per 65% lower Lp-PLA2 activity: Val279Phe 0.95 (0.88-1.03); any LoF 0.92 (0.74-1.16); Val379Ala 1.01 (0.68-1.51); darapladib trials 0.95 (0.89-1.02)
genetics.quote: Causal risk ratios for coronary heart disease per 65% lower Lp-PLA2 activity were: 0.95 (0.88-1.03) with Val279Phe; 0.92 (0.74-1.16) with carriage of any loss-of-function variant; 1.01 (0.68-1.51) with Val379Ala; and 0.95 (0.89-1.02) with darapladib treatment.
genetics.note: Online first 2016-12-08; post-dates both darapladib readouts.

consensus_explanation.summary: Second, independent null darapladib outcome trial (HR 1.00 for major coronary events, and 0.99 for the original MACE end point), confirming STABILITY in a post-ACS population despite the end point being switched to the one that looked favourable in STABILITY. Darapladib inhibits plasma Lp-PLA2 by ~65% (phase 2; STABILITY on-treatment), so the failure is not explained by inadequate target engagement. Subsequent human genetics (Millwood 2016 V279F; Gregson 2017 five PLA2G7 alleles) showed genetically lower Lp-PLA2 activity does not reduce CHD, with a causal estimate per 65% lower activity (~0.95) matching the pooled trial result. Consensus: Lp-PLA2 is a non-causal risk marker; the target was invalid. Pre-trial genetic evidence (Casas 2010) was too weak to test causality.

available_before_readout: Design: ~13,000 patients, ~1,500 events, 90% power, 15.5% RRR (S2 American Heart Journal, online 2011-09-15; abstract free)
Registry record with eligibility (S3, first posted 2009-10-23)
Phase 2 Lp-PLA2 inhibition ~66% at 160 mg (S7, 2008-04-29); IBIS-2 -59% with negative primary end points (S8, 2008-09-01)

STABILITY failure: top-line 2013-11-12 (S6) and full NEJM results 2014-03-30 (S5) - an informative null result in a closely related population with the same drug and dose, available ~6 months before SOLID readout
Primary end point switch to major coronary events (decided Dec 2013) - disclosed publicly only in JAMA 2014-08-31 (S1); GSK headline release (S4) named MCE as the primary end point
Genetics: Casas 2010 (S9) weak instrument, null; Yamada 2000 (S12)
only_after_readout: Full results HR 1.00 (0.91-1.09), 903 vs 910 events, median follow-up 2.5 y, end point amendment details (S1 JAMA 2014-08-31)

access_summary.note: Counted by best free access. Open full text (JAMA S1, read via WebFetch without login; jamanetwork.com blocks curl and shows a Cloudflare bot check in a browser): N, median follow-up, planned events, RRR, power, alpha, HR, CI x2, p, events x2, baseline Lp-PLA2. All outcome numbers are also in the free abstract and registry results; planned events/power/RRR also in the free design abstract (S2). Abstract only: phase 2 Lp-PLA2 (S7), IBIS-2 (S8). Not found: on-treatment Lp-PLA2 reduction in SOLID-TIMI 52.

open_questions: On-treatment Lp-PLA2 activity reduction in SOLID-TIMI 52: NOT FOUND in the JAMA paper (only 'anticipated an approximate 66% reduction'). The secondary figure '~-66%' appears to come from the phase 2 study (Mohler 2008) or pooled trials (Gregson 2017: 65%). A dedicated SOLID biomarker paper was not found.

Primary end point changed (Dec 2013) from CV death/MI/stroke to major coronary events after seeing STABILITY results, while SOLID was still blinded. Planned events (1500) and power refer to the original end point; JAMA says the change 'did not substantially affect the power'. No revised event target found.

JAMA full text access: WebFetch returned full text without login, but curl gets HTTP 403 and the browser shows a Cloudflare 'verify you are not a bot' page. Europe PMC: not open access, no PMC copy. Classified open_full_text with this caveat; JAMA verbatim quotes beyond the abstract came through WebFetch extraction (small-model relay), so minor wording differences are possible.
Baseline Lp-PLA2 quote is a reconstruction of a Table 1 row, not running text.
Online publication date: JAMA lists 'Published Online: August 31, 2014'; Europe PMC firstPublicationDate 2014-09-01 (PubMed entry date).
